article_title: ‘Supporting socially shared regulation during collaborative task-oriented reading’
citation: Kielstra, J., Molenaar, I., van Steensel, R., & Verhoeven, L. (2022). 'Supporting socially shared regulation during collaborative task‑oriented reading'. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning, 17, 65–105. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-022-09365-x
title: 'Y-read?' digital learning environment with a macro- and micro-level collaboration script for socially shared regulation of task-oriented reading
description: 'Y-read?' is a digital learning environment integrating a collaboration script and the TOR-test, built from four script elements: play, scene, scriptlets and roles. The "macro-level script combines the components 'play', 'scene' and 'roles'" and guides four scenes: pre-task group planning, individual task execution, individual reflection and post-task group reflection. A stated novelty is "a full automation flow of role information and related learning materials to different participants on four different tablets that synchronously drive face-to-face collaboration". Roles were rotated across four lessons.
requirements: Students collaborate face-to-face in groups of four, each with their own device; information distribution follows the Jigsaw distributed-information principle to elicit interdependency.
constraints: Only pre- and post-task regulation was performed collaboratively; task execution and individual reflection were individual phases.
target_learners: prevocational secondary school students (10th grade, average age 15.7)
target_learning_goals: metacognitive regulation of task-oriented reading: task representation, strategy selection, strategy reflection
examples: During pre-task planning, the leader received guiding questions, the writer recorded task-representation ratings on 1–10 scales, the task guard held the task, and the text guard a blurred text showing only title, headers and pictures.
